scope: Master of Fighters / Dr. Social 61-pose basic animation source
observation: Global nearest-RGB palette quantization can be palette-legal yet semantically wrong: v05 showed boot-brown/burgundy in gray hair and v06 still spread burgundy into the coat, cane-adjacent pixels and boots; effect-only red and tiny blue-ramp islands also harmed the neutral movement palette. v07 reduced burgundy from 4,182 to 793 pixels by retaining it only in the cravat/cuff zones.
practices_to_consider: Review palette roles by material, not only by palette index count or RGB closure.
Exclude effect-only colors from neutral movement states unless a frame contract explicitly calls for the effect.
Inspect enlarged nearest-neighbor crops of face, hair, costume, cane grip, and terminal—not only the full-sheet thumbnail.
Use a face/hair spatial relationship to correct head color leakage while preserving the actual face cluster.
Merge only tiny isolated shade clusters inside a declared material ramp; keep open negative spaces and do not move pose geometry.
Run a second review for palette-role leakage after silhouette/alpha cleanup; structural gates do not judge anatomy or material identity.
Constrain semantic accents by garment geometry: follow the face-to-upper-torso axis for a cravat and preserve cuffs only between a compact glove cluster and the body-facing sleeve side.
Reject elongated staff/cane clusters as glove anchors so material-role cleanup cannot tint equipment.
After local recoloring, verify unchanged alpha masks, frame count/order, cell margins and every palette role at native size and nearest-neighbor enlargement.
limitations: This candidate lesson does not modify the canonical agent or SMS_GLOBAL. Algorithmic role confinement is not proof that every remaining accent is artistically correct; anatomy, pixel clusters, palette semantics, pose timing, hardware budget, ROM behavior and owner approval remain pending.
